summary: Christian Gottlob Heyne (1729–1812) was a linguist, historian, and archaeologist who earned his master's degree at the University of Leipzig (1748–1752). He served as Professor at the University of Göttingen (1763) and Director of its library (1764–1812).

Christian K. Wedemeyer is a scholar of Buddhist, Tibetan, and religious studies. He studied at Wesleyan University and Columbia University (M.A., Ph.D.) under Robert A. F. Thurman, later teaching at the University of Copenhagen and the University of Chicago.

Christian Lassen (1800–1876) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Oslo, Heidelberg, and Bonn, the latter under August Wilhelm von Schlegel. He served at the University of Bonn as Privatdozent (1830) and ordentlicher Professor (1840–1876).

Christian Lee Novetzke is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Macalester College, Harvard University, and Columbia University. He taught at the University of Pennsylvania (2003–2007) and became Director of the South Asia Center at the University of Washington in 2007.

Christian Lindtner (1949–2020) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He received his doctoral degree from the University of Copenhagen (1982), where he also held a professorship attested from 1980 to 1991.

Christian Luczanits is a scholar in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his Magister and Ph.D. at the University of Vienna, served as Curator at the Rubin Museum of Art (attested 2012), and held visiting professorships at Stanford and UC Berkeley.

Christian Matthias Boehm works in Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of John T. Carpenter (attested 2005) and also studied under Toshifumi Konno.

Christian Parker Haskett is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied under Robert A. F. Thurman and completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2010), later holding a post at Washington and Lee University.

Christian Wittern works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and computational fields. He studied under Seizan Yanagida and held posts as Professor at Kyoto University and its Institute for Research in Humanities (attested 1993), as well as at Hanazono University (attested 2011).

Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck (1866–1951) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Leiden University (c. 1883–1888). He served as an assistant professor at the University of Amsterdam (1892–1899) and as professor at Leiden University (1899–1926).
Christine Chojnacki is an Indologist who completed her doctoral thesis at Sorbonne Nouvelle University in 1991. She served as Professor at Jean Moulin University Lyon 3, attested in 2018.

Christine Mollier is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied under Kristofer Schipper and Michel Soymié. She worked as a researcher and Director of Research at the CNRS (1989–1995, attested 2014) and visited the University of Chicago.

Christmas Humphreys (1901–1983) was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Malvern College and Trinity Hall, Cambridge, and served as President of the Buddhist Society from circa 1924 to 1983.

Christoph Anderl is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and linguistics. He completed an MA at the University of Vienna and a PhD at the University of Oslo under Christoph Harbsmeier, later joining Ghent University circa 2012.

Christoph Cüppers is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Hamburg (1973–1983) under Lambert Schmithausen and served as Director of the Lumbini International Research Institute from circa 1993 to 2013.

Christoph Emmrich is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies scholar. He completed his PhD at Heidelberg University under Axel Michaels in 2004, held a post at Heidelberg (attested 2001), and served as Assistant Professor at the University of Toronto (attested 2026).

Christoph Harbsmeier is a sinologist and linguist who studied at Oxford (Merton College) and the University of Copenhagen (Ph.D.). He held posts at Universiti Sains Malaysia and the University of Oslo, alongside advisory professorships at Peking, Fudan, and Shanghai Normal universities.

Christoph Kleine is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Marburg (MA, PhD, Habilitation) and held professorships at the University of Munich (2004–2008) and the University of Leipzig (appointed 2008).

Christoph Theodosius Walther (1699–1741) was an Indologist and linguist who studied theology at the University of Halle in 1720. He served as a missionary with the Tranquebar Mission from circa 1725 to 1739.

Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf (1909–1995) was an anthropologist and historian who studied at Vienna and the LSE under Leo Frobenius. He was a professor at Osmania University (1945) and held the Chair of Asian Anthropology at the University of London (1951–1976).
